title: Statistical process control: u-, p- and individuals charts
summary: Control charts for an infection rate, a readmission proportion and mean length of stay, with limits set from a baseline and applied forward.

sizing._why: Control charts are not sized; the baseline needs enough periods (20 to 25 is common) for stable limits.

pinned_defaults: u-chart for counts over exposure, p-chart for proportions, individuals (XmR) chart with sigma = mean moving range / 1.128; 3-sigma limits; baseline months 1 to 12 applied to all 24. R qcc (newdata for months 13 to 24); Python written out.
A signal is a point beyond a limit; run rules are not applied.
_baseline: Limits from a 12-month baseline are themselves uncertain: over 100 seeds the steady p- and individuals charts gave 0.47 false signals per 48 chart-months (about 1% per point against the nominal 0.27%), and the u-chart signalled before the rise in 5% of seeds. Use 20 to 25 baseline points where possible.
_rare_events: A first fixture with 2 to 3 infections a month never signalled when the rate doubled: SPC is insensitive to changes in rare events at 3-sigma. The fixture uses a larger exposure and a rise from 2 to 5 per 1,000 catheter-days.
